name: Hydroxychloroquine
route_note: oral tablets once or twice daily; long-term use for autoimmune disease with retinal screening
targets: Endosomal Toll-like receptors (TLR7, TLR9) and lysosomal acidification
owner: generic (many); Plaquenil by Sanofi/Concordia (varies by region)

discovery.by: Alexander Surrey and Henry Hammer, Sterling-Winthrop
discovery.note: Hydroxylated analogue of chloroquine designed to be less toxic.

tagline: Antimalarial turned lupus mainstay, briefly at the centre of the COVID-19 storm
summary: Hydroxychloroquine is a less toxic hydroxylated analogue of chloroquine. Although developed as an antimalarial, it is used mainly as a long-term treatment for systemic lupus erythematosus, rheumatoid arthritis and other autoimmune diseases. In 2020 it was widely promoted for COVID-19, but large randomised trials showed no benefit.
mechanism: Hydroxychloroquine is a weak base that accumulates in acidic compartments such as lysosomes and endosomes, raising their pH. This interferes with antigen processing and presentation on MHC class II and inhibits signalling by endosomal Toll-like receptors (TLR7 and TLR9) that sense nucleic acids, reducing production of type I interferon and other cytokines that drive lupus.
Against malaria it acts like chloroquine, accumulating in the parasite's food vacuole and blocking conversion of toxic haem to haemozoin.
uses: Systemic and chronic discoid lupus erythematosus
Malaria treatment and prophylaxis where chloroquine-sensitive
Other rheumatological and dermatological conditions (e.g. Sjögren's disease, antiphospholipid syndrome; off-label)

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: Plaquenil is approved in the US.

history.title: Lupus evidence
history.detail: The Canadian Hydroxychloroquine Study Group shows that stopping the drug increases lupus flares (NEJM).

history.title: Retinal screening
history.detail: The American Academy of Ophthalmology revises screening guidance, recommending a dose of at most 5 mg/kg real body weight per day.

history.title: COVID-19
history.detail: The FDA grants emergency use authorisation in March and revokes it in June; the RECOVERY and WHO Solidarity trials show no mortality benefit, and shortages affect lupus patients.

pk.metabolism: hepatic CYP2C8, CYP3A4 and CYP2D6 to active desethyl metabolites

serious: irreversible retinopathy (risk rises with dose and duration)

facts: Hydroxychloroquine is a foundation therapy for systemic lupus erythematosus and is generally continued during pregnancy.
Its very long half-life means steady state is reached only after several months.

references.title: RECOVERY Collaborative Group. Effect of hydroxychloroquine in hospitalized patients with Covid-19. NEJM 2020
